scenes.visual: Big navy hook text pops word by word; Norb peeks curious from below.
scenes.cardText: Why is losing $50 worse than finding $50 feels good?
scenes.voiceover: Why does losing fifty dollars feel worse than finding fifty dollars feels good?

scenes.visual: Two side-by-side meters: the coral LOSS bar springs much higher than the teal GAIN bar — same amount, totally different emotional height.
scenes.voiceover: Your brain isn't a calculator. Losing something hurts roughly twice as much as gaining the same thing feels good.

scenes.visual: A coral pit swallows mustard coins in a loop while a teal figure stands frozen — sunk cost trap.
scenes.voiceover: So you hold on — to bad stocks, bad jobs, bad relationships — trying to recover what's already gone. That money left the building.

scenes.visual: A navy card flips from coral 'LOSE 40%' to teal 'KEEP 60%' — same deal, different frame, teal tick pops in.
scenes.voiceover: The trick is reframing. 'I'll lose 40%' and 'I'll keep 60%' are the same deal — but one feels like a win.

scenes.visual: THE SCIENCE card; below it the two-meter chart shows LOSS towering over GAIN — loss aversion quantified.
scenes.cardText: Loss aversion: losses feel about twice as powerful as equivalent gains.
scenes.voiceover: Loss aversion: research shows the pain of losing is about twice as powerful as the pleasure of an equivalent gain.

scenes.visual: TRY THIS card; below it the gain-frame card flips to show KEEP 60%. Norb celebrates.
scenes.cardText:
Before any hard decision:
ask 'what am I keeping?' not 'what could I lose?'
scenes.voiceover: Before any tough decision, ask what you are keeping — not what you might lose. Same facts, better brain.
